correctness.rationale: The quantifiers are \(b\ge2\) and \(b\not\equiv1\pmod3\). The distinct-powers theorem reduces reachability to triples \(x,y,z\ge0\) with \(x+by+b^2z\equiv0\pmod{b^2+b+1}\). Explicit triples yield the generators \(3\), \(b+2\), and \(2b+1\), which cover every integer at least \(2b-1\). For a hypothetical witness at \(2b-2\), subtracting the minimum coordinate and cyclically permuting residues yields \(n=t' +(b-1)y'\); the size bounds force an auxiliary integer \(k=1\), hence \(t'=b+2\), contradicting the required residue modulo \(3\) unless \(b\equiv1\pmod3\). The packaged regression verifier returns VERIFY_OK on all admissible bases through \(100\); the finite replay is not used as the universal proof.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a sharp closed Frobenius number for the natural first nontrivial cyclotomic order family \(n=\Phi_3(b)\), directly advancing a published exact-Frobenius question. The parameter family is structurally motivated by the order-three identity \(b^3\equiv1\pmod{\Phi_3(b)}\), and the result identifies both a last gap and a complete tail rather than reporting a bounded computation.
